```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-load}
mod <- readModelDb("Jiang_2019_iopamidol")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0219605>
* PubMed Central: <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6619810/>

`r ui$description`

Jiang 2019 adapts a two-compartment kidney model, first developed for
gadolinium MRI in mice, to dynamic contrast-enhanced CT (DCE-CT) in patients.
After a central venous bolus of iopamidol-370 (0.5 mL/kg), 45 CT acquisitions
over about 145 s follow the contrast through the abdominal aorta, the renal
parenchyma and the renal papilla. The increase in CT number above the
pre-contrast baseline is used as the iodine concentration (CT enhancement is
linear in iodine concentration). The model has no dose: the kidney is driven by
two measured curves.

| nlmixr2lib name | Paper symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CP_IOPAMIDOL_HU` (covariate) | `Ca(t)` | Aortic whole-blood enhancement (arterial input function), HU |
| `cp_aif` | `Cp(t)` | Plasma input, `Ca(t) / (1 - Hct)` with `Hct = 0.45` |
| `vp_kidney` (state) / `cv_kidney` | `Cv(t)` | Renal vascular plasma enhancement; `cv_kidney = delay(vp_kidney, Td)` |
| `kidney` (state) | `Ct(t)` | Tubular enhancement per unit kidney volume |
| `CPAPILLA_TUBULAR_IOPAMIDOL_HU` (covariate) | `Cout''(t)` | Tubular (filtration) component of the papilla curve, HU |
| `Cc` | `Ctot(t)` | Whole-kidney enhancement, `f * Cv(t) + Ct(t)`, HU |
| `gfr`, `perfusion_kidney`, `rbf_kidney` | GFR, perfusion, RBF | Derived single-kidney function (Eqs. 3-4) |

# Population

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

Thirty-eight hypertensive adults (Jiang 2019 Table 1) studied as inpatients at
the Mayo Clinic, Rochester, MN, on ACE-inhibitor or angiotensin-receptor-blocker
therapy and a fixed 150 mEq/day sodium diet: 13 with essential hypertension (EH;
26 kidneys) and 25 with atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis (ARAS; 30 stenotic
and 20 contralateral kidneys, 5 patients with bilateral stenosis). Median age 67
(EH) and 70 (ARAS) years; 22 of 38 were male. Serum creatinine had to be below
2.5 mg/dL. The kidney, not the patient, is the unit of the model: every kidney
was fitted separately.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Vascular equation | `dCv/dt = kperf (Cp(t - Td) - Cv)` | Eq. 1 |
| Tubular equation | `dCt/dt = kGFR Cv - kout Cout''(t)` | Eq. 2 |
| Plasma input | `Cp = Ca / (1 - Hct)`, `Hct = 0.45` | Methods, Compartment model |
| Kidney signal | `Ctot = Cv f + Ct` | Methods, after Fig 2 |
| GFR | `kGFR * V * 60` (mL/min) | Eq. 3 |
| Perfusion | `kperf * f * 60 * 100 / (1 - Hct) * sigma` (mL/100 g/min), `sigma = 0.9` | Eq. 4 |
| Renal blood flow | perfusion * V / 100 (mL/min) | Methods, after Eq. 4 |
| `kperf` EH / stenotic / contralateral | 0.15 / 0.12 / 0.17 1/s (medians) | Table 2 |
| `Td` EH / stenotic / contralateral | 0.68 / 0.58 / 1.02 s (medians) | Table 2 |
| `f` EH / stenotic / contralateral | 0.22 / 0.19 / 0.18 (means) | Table 2 |
| `kGFR` EH / stenotic / contralateral | 0.0048 / 0.0035 / 0.0041 1/s (means) | Table 2 |
| `kout` EH / stenotic / contralateral | 0.004 / 0.005 / 0.007 1/s (medians) | Table 2 |
| Residual error | none reported (least-squares fit); `addSd` fixed at 0 | Methods, Image analysis |

```{r ini-table}
ui$iniDf |>
  dplyr::select(name, est, fix, label) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

# The S1 Dataset

The paper's S1 Dataset (an Excel workbook, CC BY) holds, for every kidney, the
raw aortic, kidney and papilla time-attenuation curves and the fitted model
parameters. Both are shipped next to this article as CSV files.

```{r load-data}
curves <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "Jiang_2019_iopamidol_curves.csv"))
fits <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "Jiang_2019_iopamidol_fits.csv"))
grp_levels <- c("EH", "stenotic", "contralateral")
curves$group <- factor(curves$group, levels = grp_levels)
fits$group <- factor(fits$group, levels = grp_levels)
stopifnot(
  identical(as.vector(table(fits$group)), c(26L, 30L, 20L)),
  identical(as.vector(table(curves$group)) / 45, c(26, 30, 20))
)
```

The workbook stores raw CT numbers with the scanner's +1024 offset. The
enhancement is the CT number minus the mean of the first three scans
(0-2 s, before the bolus reaches the aorta).

```{r baseline}
curves <- curves |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, kidney) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ca = aorta_hu - mean(aorta_hu[time <= 2]),
    ctot_obs = kidney_hu - mean(kidney_hu[time <= 2]),
    cout = papilla_hu - mean(papilla_hu[time <= 2])
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

## Transcription check: Table 2 against the per-kidney fits

Recomputing the Table 2 summaries from the per-kidney fits checks the
packaged values. In the workbook the kidney-type column labels the last five
stenotic kidneys `CLK`; they are counted here by the workbook section they sit
in (30 stenotic, 20 contralateral), which matches the counts in the paper.

```{r table2-check}
med_iqr <- function(x, digits) {
  sprintf(
    paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f-%.", digits, "f)"),
    median(x), quantile(x, 0.25), quantile(x, 0.75)
  )
}
mean_sd <- function(x, digits) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f +/- %.", digits, "f"), mean(x), sd(x))
}
recomputed <- fits |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Volume (mL)` = mean_sd(volume_ml, 0),
    `kperf (1/s)` = med_iqr(kperf, 2),
    `Td (s)` = med_iqr(td, 2),
    f = mean_sd(f, 2),
    `kGFR (1/s)` = mean_sd(kgfr, 4),
    `kout (1/s)` = med_iqr(kout, 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
published <- tibble::tibble(
  group = factor(grp_levels, levels = grp_levels),
  `Volume (mL)` = c("148 +/- 33", "86 +/- 44", "170 +/- 50"),
  `kperf (1/s)` = c("0.15 (0.11-0.19)", "0.12 (0.09-0.17)", "0.17 (0.11-0.18)"),
  `Td (s)` = c("0.68 (0.34-1.16)", "0.58 (0.05-1.35)", "1.02 (0.47-1.57)"),
  f = c("0.22 +/- 0.04", "0.19 +/- 0.06", "0.18 +/- 0.04"),
  `kGFR (1/s)` = c("0.0048 +/- 0.0009", "0.0035 +/- 0.0013", "0.0041 +/- 0.0011"),
  `kout (1/s)` = c("0.004 (0.003-0.011)", "0.005 (0.003-0.012)", "0.007 (0.002-0.009)")
)
dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(published, Source = "Table 2"),
  dplyr::mutate(recomputed, Source = "S1 Dataset")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(group, Source) |>
  dplyr::relocate(Source, .after = group) |>
  dplyr::rename(Kidney = group) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r table2-gate}
pkg <- setNames(ui$iniDf$est, ui$iniDf$name)
grp_sfx <- c(EH = "eh", stenotic = "sten", contralateral = "contra")
gate <- fits |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    kperf = median(kperf), td = median(td), f = mean(f), kgfr = mean(kgfr),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gate))) {
  s <- grp_sfx[[as.character(gate$group[i])]]
  # kperf and f are printed to 2 decimals and kGFR to 4: the recomputed value
  # must round to the packaged one (half a unit in the last printed place).
  stopifnot(
    abs(gate$kperf[i] - pkg[[paste0("kperf_kidney_", s)]]) <= 0.005 + 1e-9,
    abs(gate$f[i] - pkg[[paste0("fvasc_kidney_", s)]]) <= 0.005 + 1e-9,
    abs(gate$kgfr[i] - pkg[[paste0("kgfr_kidney_", s)]]) <= 0.00005 + 1e-9
  )
}
```

The central values of `kperf`, `f` and `kGFR` (the gated quantities) recompute
to the printed values in all three groups, and so do the EH and contralateral
volumes and `Td`. The remaining differences are recorded under Assumptions and
deviations; the largest are the stenotic kidney volume (95 vs 86 mL printed),
the stenotic `Td` median (0.52 vs 0.58 s) and the EH `kout` (median 0.003 with
IQR 0.000-0.009, printed 0.004 (0.003-0.011)). The packaged model carries the
printed Table 2 values.

## Derived outputs: Eqs. 3 and 4

The packaged model computes single-kidney GFR, perfusion and renal blood flow as
algebraic outputs. Solving it once per kidney with that kidney's fitted
parameters reproduces the workbook's own GFR and perfusion columns.

```{r derived}
fits$id <- seq_len(nrow(fits))
derived_ev <- fits |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, time = 0, evid = 0, CP_IOPAMIDOL_HU = 0, CPAPILLA_TUBULAR_IOPAMIDOL_HU = 0,
    DIS_RAS_STENOTIC = 0, DIS_RAS_CONTRALATERAL = 0, ORGVOL_KIDNEY = volume_ml
  )
# Every kidney is routed through the EH slot of the model, whose parameters are
# overridden with that kidney's own fitted values.
derived_par <- fits |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, kperf_kidney_eh = kperf, tdelay_kidney_eh = td, fvasc_kidney_eh = f,
    kgfr_kidney_eh = kgfr, kout_tubule_eh = kout
  )
derived <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = derived_ev, params = derived_par, returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fits, by = "id")
derived <- derived |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    rel_gfr = gfr / gfr_ct - 1,
    rel_perf = perfusion_kidney / perfusion - 1
  )
# Eq. 3 reproduces the workbook GFR for 69 of the 76 kidneys and Eq. 4 the
# workbook perfusion for 70 (relative difference below 1e-5, the CSV carries 7
# significant figures); the rest were evidently computed from a different
# parameter set (differences of 1% to 74%), so the gate counts exact matches
# rather than demanding all of them.
stopifnot(
  sum(abs(derived$rel_gfr) < 1e-5) >= 65,
  sum(abs(derived$rel_perf) < 1e-5) >= 65
)
derived |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `GFR model (mL/min)` = med_iqr(gfr, 1),
    `Perfusion model (mL/100 g/min)` = med_iqr(perfusion_kidney, 1),
    `RBF model (mL/min)` = med_iqr(rbf_kidney, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `GFR text` = c("40.4 (36.1-50.9)", "20.0 (8.4-26.6)", "41.2 (28.3-50.9)"),
    `Perfusion text` = c("308.1 (261.6-385.7)", "194.8 (162.0-290.2)", "280.8 (191.8-310.6)"),
    `RBF text` = c("463.3 (398.1-639.0)", "182.0 (130.0-274.1)", "456.2 (282.3-579.6)")
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(Kidney = group) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The EH GFR median matches the Results text (40.4 mL/min). The perfusion and
RBF summaries differ from the text by up to about 8%, because seven workbook
rows carry a perfusion value that does not follow Eq. 4 from that row's own
`kperf` and `f`; the text was evidently computed from the workbook column (its
EH perfusion median recomputes to exactly 308.1 mL/100 g/min). The stenotic and
contralateral GFR medians differ slightly, in line with the per-kidney
differences noted above.

# Structural validation against the published curves

The S1 curve rows and fitted-parameter rows are not in the same kidney order
(a curve is fitted best by the parameters of a different row), so a kidney's
published fit cannot be paired with its curve. Instead, the model structure is
validated by re-fitting every curve and comparing the re-fitted parameters with
Table 2.

## The papilla tubular component

`Cout''(t)` is not tabulated. Following the Methods, the papilla curve is split
into a perfusion component, `a * Cvp(t)`, where `Cvp` solves Eq. 1 for the
papilla with its own rate constant, and the remainder. `a` and the papilla rate
constant are fitted to the papilla curve over 0-30 s (before filtered contrast
arrives), the perfusion component is subtracted, negative values are set to 0,
and the remainder is set to 0 before 20 s.

The re-fit uses an independent reference implementation of Eqs. 1-2 on a
0.1 s grid: the first-order equation is advanced exactly for a piecewise-linear
input, the delay is applied by interpolation, and `Ct` is integrated by the
trapezoidal rule.

```{r reference-implementation}
ref_h <- 0.1
ref_grid <- seq(0, 146, by = ref_h)

# Exact one-step update of dy/dt = k (u - y) for u linear within the step.
first_order <- function(u, k, h = ref_h) {
  e <- exp(-k * h)
  a <- (1 - e) / (k * h)
  inc <- u[-1] * (1 - a) + u[-length(u)] * (a - e)
  c(0, as.numeric(stats::filter(inc, e, method = "recursive", init = 0)))
}
shift_delay <- function(y, td, grid = ref_grid) {
  stats::approx(grid, y, grid - td, yleft = 0, rule = 2)$y
}
ref_predict <- function(kperf, td, f, kgfr, kout, cp_grid, cout2_grid, times,
                        h = ref_h, grid = ref_grid) {
  cv <- shift_delay(first_order(cp_grid, kperf, h), td, grid)
  dct <- kgfr * cv - kout * cout2_grid
  ct <- c(0, cumsum((dct[-1] + dct[-length(dct)]) / 2 * h))
  stats::approx(grid, f * cv + ct, times)$y
}
# Papilla perfusion component (unit amplitude) for a papilla rate constant exp(lk).
papilla_shape <- function(lk, cp_grid, times) {
  stats::approx(ref_grid, first_order(cp_grid, exp(lk)), times)$y
}
# Least-squares amplitude of the perfusion component over the early window.
papilla_amplitude <- function(v, cout, early) {
  sum(v[early] * cout[early]) / sum(v[early]^2)
}
papilla_sse <- function(lk, cp_grid, times, cout, early) {
  v <- papilla_shape(lk, cp_grid, times)
  a <- papilla_amplitude(v, cout, early)
  sum((cout[early] - a * v[early])^2)
}
papilla_tubular <- function(d, hct = 0.45) {
  cp_grid <- stats::approx(d$time, d$ca / (1 - hct), ref_grid, rule = 2)$y
  early <- d$time <= 30
  lk <- stats::optimize(
    papilla_sse, c(log(0.005), log(3)),
    cp_grid = cp_grid, times = d$time, cout = d$cout, early = early
  )$minimum
  v <- papilla_shape(lk, cp_grid, d$time)
  out <- pmax(d$cout - papilla_amplitude(v, d$cout, early) * v, 0)
  out[d$time < 20] <- 0
  out
}
curves <- curves |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, kidney) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(~ dplyr::mutate(.x, cout2 = papilla_tubular(.x))) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

## Packaged model against the reference implementation

```{r model-vs-reference}
sel_kidneys <- curves |>
  dplyr::filter((group == "EH" & kidney == 1) | (group == "stenotic" & kidney == 1) |
    (group == "contralateral" & kidney == 1)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(group))
mvr_ev <- sel_kidneys |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, time, evid = 0,
    CP_IOPAMIDOL_HU = ca, CPAPILLA_TUBULAR_IOPAMIDOL_HU = cout2,
    DIS_RAS_STENOTIC = as.integer(group == "stenotic"),
    DIS_RAS_CONTRALATERAL = as.integer(group == "contralateral"),
    ORGVOL_KIDNEY = 150
  )
mvr <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = mvr_ev, covsInterpolation = "linear",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-10, returnType = "data.frame"
)
fine_h <- 0.005
fine_grid <- seq(0, 146, by = fine_h)
ref_typical <- sel_kidneys |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, group) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(function(d, key) {
    s <- grp_sfx[[as.character(key$group)]]
    cp_grid <- stats::approx(d$time, d$ca / (1 - pkg[["hct"]]), fine_grid, rule = 2)$y
    c2_grid <- stats::approx(d$time, d$cout2, fine_grid, rule = 2)$y
    tibble::tibble(
      time = d$time,
      ref = ref_predict(
        pkg[[paste0("kperf_kidney_", s)]], pkg[[paste0("tdelay_kidney_", s)]],
        pkg[[paste0("fvasc_kidney_", s)]], pkg[[paste0("kgfr_kidney_", s)]],
        pkg[[paste0("kout_tubule_", s)]], cp_grid, c2_grid, d$time,
        h = fine_h, grid = fine_grid
      )
    )
  }) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
mvr_cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(mvr, ref_typical, by = c("id", "time"))
stopifnot(nrow(mvr_cmp) == nrow(mvr_ev))
max_abs_diff <- max(abs(mvr_cmp$Cc - mvr_cmp$ref))
max_abs_diff
# Both sides use the same parameters and inputs, so the difference is numerical
# only: the reference's trapezoid and grid interpolation at 0.005 s against the
# ODE solver. The kidney signal peaks near 100-200 HU.
stopifnot(max_abs_diff < 0.05)
```

## Re-fit of all 76 kidneys

Each kidney curve is re-fitted over 0-120 s by least squares (the paper used
Levenberg-Marquardt; `optim()` L-BFGS-B is used here) starting from the EH
values of Table 2.

```{r refit}
# th = (log kperf, Td, f, log kGFR, kout)
kidney_sse <- function(th, cp_grid, c2_grid, times, obs, win) {
  p <- ref_predict(exp(th[1]), th[2], th[3], exp(th[4]), th[5], cp_grid, c2_grid, times)
  sum((obs[win] - p[win])^2)
}
refit_one <- function(d, hct = 0.45) {
  cp_grid <- stats::approx(d$time, d$ca / (1 - hct), ref_grid, rule = 2)$y
  c2_grid <- stats::approx(d$time, d$cout2, ref_grid, rule = 2)$y
  win <- d$time <= 121
  o <- stats::optim(
    c(log(0.15), 0.68, 0.22, log(0.0048), 0.004), kidney_sse, method = "L-BFGS-B",
    lower = c(log(0.01), 0, 0.01, log(1e-5), 0), upper = c(log(2), 5, 0.6, log(0.05), 0.2),
    cp_grid = cp_grid, c2_grid = c2_grid, times = d$time, obs = d$ctot_obs, win = win
  )
  sst <- sum((d$ctot_obs[win] - mean(d$ctot_obs[win]))^2)
  tibble::tibble(
    kperf = exp(o$par[1]), td = o$par[2], f = o$par[3], kgfr = exp(o$par[4]),
    kout = o$par[5], R = sqrt(max(0, 1 - o$value / sst))
  )
}
refit <- curves |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, kidney) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(~ refit_one(.x)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
refit_summary <- refit |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `kperf (1/s)` = med_iqr(kperf, 2),
    `Td (s)` = med_iqr(td, 2),
    f = mean_sd(f, 2),
    `kGFR median (1/s)` = sprintf("%.4f", median(kgfr)),
    `kout (1/s)` = med_iqr(kout, 3),
    `R` = mean_sd(R, 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
refit_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Table 2 kGFR mean (1/s)` = c("0.0048", "0.0035", "0.0041"),
    `Paper R` = c("0.94 +/- 0.06", "0.93 +/- 0.12", "0.95 +/- 0.07")
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(Kidney = group) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r refit-gate}
refit_gate <- refit |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(kgfr = median(kgfr), R = mean(R), .groups = "drop")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(refit_gate))) {
  s <- grp_sfx[[as.character(refit_gate$group[i])]]
  stopifnot(
    # The model structure applied to the published curves fits them as well as
    # the paper reports (multiple correlation coefficient near 0.94).
    refit_gate$R[i] > 0.9,
    # The re-fitted median kGFR, the parameter GFR is computed from, lands
    # within 20% of Table 2 (measured: within 10% in all three groups).
    abs(refit_gate$kgfr[i] / pkg[[paste0("kgfr_kidney_", s)]] - 1) < 0.2
  )
}
# The paper's main finding: stenotic kidneys filter less than EH kidneys.
stopifnot(refit_gate$kgfr[refit_gate$group == "stenotic"] <
  refit_gate$kgfr[refit_gate$group == "EH"])
```

The re-fit is deterministic (no random numbers). The structure fits the
published curves with a multiple correlation coefficient at least as high as the
paper's, and the re-fitted `kGFR`, the parameter GFR is derived from,
reproduces Table 2. `kperf` and `Td` move more: they are traded off against
each other on the sharp vascular peak, and they depend on the reconstructed
papilla component and on the input interpolation, which the paper does not
fully specify.

# Typical-value simulation

The three kidney groups are simulated with their Table 2 values, all driven by
the same measured inputs (EH kidney 1 of the S1 Dataset), to separate the
vascular and tubular components as in Fig 2c (right).

```{r typical, fig.cap = "Typical kidneys of the three groups, all driven by the aortic and papilla curves of EH kidney 1 (S1 Dataset). Circles: that kidney's measured enhancement. Compare Fig 2c (right) of Jiang 2019."}
drive <- curves |> dplyr::filter(group == "EH", kidney == 1)
typ_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(grp_levels), function(i) {
  tibble::tibble(
    id = i, time = drive$time, evid = 0,
    CP_IOPAMIDOL_HU = drive$ca, CPAPILLA_TUBULAR_IOPAMIDOL_HU = drive$cout2,
    DIS_RAS_STENOTIC = as.integer(i == 2), DIS_RAS_CONTRALATERAL = as.integer(i == 3),
    ORGVOL_KIDNEY = c(148, 86, 170)[i]
  )
}))
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = typ_ev, covsInterpolation = "linear", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    group = factor(grp_levels[id], levels = grp_levels),
    vascular = fvasc_kidney * cv_kidney
  )
typ |>
  dplyr::select(group, time, `Whole kidney` = Cc, Vascular = vascular, Tubular = kidney) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(group, time), names_to = "component", values_to = "hu") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, hu, colour = component)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = drive |> dplyr::mutate(group = factor("EH", levels = grp_levels)),
    aes(time, ctot_obs), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 1, size = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (s)", y = "Kidney CT enhancement (HU)", colour = NULL
  )
```

```{r typical-derived}
typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Kidney = group,
    `GFR (mL/min)` = round(gfr, 1),
    `Perfusion (mL/100 g/min)` = round(perfusion_kidney, 1),
    `RBF (mL/min)` = round(rbf_kidney, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

These typical-kidney values are computed from group summaries (and the Table 2
mean volume), so they are not the medians of the per-kidney GFR, perfusion and
RBF reported in the Results.

```{r typical-gate}
typ_end <- typ |> dplyr::group_by(group) |> dplyr::slice_max(time, n = 1) |> dplyr::ungroup()
stopifnot(
  # Filtration accumulates contrast in the tubules: the stenotic kidney, with
  # the lowest kGFR, holds the least tubular contrast at the end of the scan.
  typ_end$kidney[typ_end$group == "stenotic"] < typ_end$kidney[typ_end$group == "EH"],
  # Eq. 3 for the typical EH kidney: 0.0048 * 148 * 60 = 42.6 mL/min.
  abs(typ$gfr[typ$group == "EH"][1] - 0.0048 * 148 * 60) < 1e-6
)
```

# PKNCA

No NCA is performed. The model has no dose and no plasma concentration-time
profile of its own: the kidney is driven by measured input curves, so Cmax, AUC
and half-life describe the input the user supplies, not the model. The
validation above (transcription check, derived-output check, solver check and
re-fit) replaces it.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Values are group summaries of individual fits.** Each kidney was fitted
  separately. The packaged parameters are the Table 2 summaries, as printed:
  medians for `kperf`, `Td` and `kout`, means for `f` and `kGFR`. No
  between-kidney random effects were estimated, so none are included, and no
  residual-error model was reported (`addSd` is fixed at 0).
* **Transit delay.** rxode2 cannot delay a covariate, so the delay of Eq. 1 is
  applied to the solution: because Eq. 1 is linear with a zero initial value,
  `Cv(t)` equals the undelayed solution at `t - Td`. The state `vp_kidney` holds
  the undelayed solution and `cv_kidney = delay(vp_kidney, tdelay_kidney)`. The
  solver check above confirms the result against a direct implementation.
* **Inputs are measured curves.** The model needs the aortic enhancement and the
  tubular component of the papilla curve as time-varying covariates (`linear()`
  interpolation, as the authors resampled the curves to 0.5 s linearly). The
  paper does not report how the papilla perfusion component was fitted beyond
  "from the early tubular phase (30 to 40 s) prior to contrast arrival using
  Eq 1"; the reconstruction in this article (fit over 0-30 s, remainder set to 0
  before 20 s) is the maintainers' choice.
* **Baseline.** The enhancement is taken relative to the mean of the first three
  scans (0-2 s). The paper states only that "the increase in CT signal from
  baseline" was used.
* **Table 2 against the S1 Dataset.** The stenotic kidney volume recomputes to
  95 +/- 50 mL (printed 86 +/- 44), the stenotic `Td` median to 0.52 s (printed
  0.58), the EH `kout` to a median of 0.0034 with IQR 0.0002-0.0095 (printed
  0.004 (0.003-0.011)) and the contralateral `kout` to 0.006 (0.002-0.008)
  (printed 0.007 (0.002-0.009)); a few SDs and IQR limits differ in the last
  printed digit. The stenotic and contralateral GFR medians recompute to 20.4
  and 42.5 mL/min (Results text 20.0 and 41.2). The printed Table 2 values are
  packaged.
* **S1 Dataset row order.** The curve rows and the fitted-parameter rows of the
  workbook are not in the same kidney order, so published fits cannot be
  replayed on their own curves; the structure is validated by re-fitting
  instead. Seven GFR and six perfusion entries of the workbook do not follow
  Eqs. 3-4 from their own row's parameters.
* **Kidney volume.** `ORGVOL_KIDNEY` is the single-kidney volume. It is used only
  by the derived GFR and renal blood flow outputs.
* **Haematocrit and sigma.** Both are the paper's fixed constants (0.45 and
  0.9 mL/g). A user with a measured haematocrit can override `hct`.
